business_patterns.top_pattern: Authorized acute hospital spend is surging in MO and recurring in other TANF Standard markets
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: Medicaid / TANF Standard / ACUTE HOSPITAL prior-authorization admissions
key_driver_codes: Postpartum and Postabortion Diagnoses without O.R. Procedures
Major Small and Large Bowel Procedures with CC
Cranial and Peripheral Nerve Disorders without MCC
business_patterns.pattern_details: MO is the dominant driver of authorized acute hospital spend growth, and the increase is not purely a volume story. Admissions rose materially and paid per admission also increased, with additional recurring pressure in CA, FL, KS, MD, OH, NC, LA, and NY. The pattern shows broad inpatient pressure in TANF Standard rather than a single isolated case.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: This is the largest operational cost pattern and points to combined utilization management and reimbursement pressure in a core Medicaid inpatient setting.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Launch a joint UM and reimbursement review for TANF Standard acute hospital admissions, starting in MO, with focused review of postpartum, pneumothorax, bowel, and nerve disorder stays where both admission counts and cost per stay increased.
evidence_summary: MO TANF Standard acute hospital claims increased about $28.6M, with 887 more admissions and about $1.4K higher paid per admission.
A broader CA, FL, KS, MD, and OH acute hospital group added about $3.9M, showing the pattern is recurring outside MO.
CA also had a separate volume-led increase of about $1.9M in TANF Standard acute hospital admissions, including 66 more admissions in major bowel procedures.
NC and LA/NY added roughly $1.0M combined, again led by higher authorized inpatient volume.

business_patterns.top_pattern: Large facility mapping gap is obscuring where authorized spend is actually occurring
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: Facility classification and provider attribution for prior-authorization claims
business_patterns.pattern_details: A large share of growth is sitting in a Not Mapped facility bucket, especially in MO and DC, which makes site-of-care and provider attribution unreliable. The same issue recurs across multiple products and also appears in provider-concentrated settings such as SENTARA NORFOLK GENERAL HOSPITAL and SAINT THOMAS WEST HOSPITAL. Business action should wait until these claims are reclassified to the correct facility setting.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: If these claims stay unmapped, site-of-care, UM, and contracting actions may target the wrong setting or provider.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Audit and reclassify Not Mapped claims first, starting with MO and DC, then clean up provider-level Not Mapped claims in VA, TN, IN, CO, and NY physical rehab before taking utilization or reimbursement action.
business_patterns.validation_reason: A material share of the increase is in Not Mapped facility records, so facility setting and provider attribution need to be confirmed before operational decisions are made.
evidence_summary: MO Not Mapped TANF Standard claims increased about $7.6M, with 446 more admissions and about $7.6K higher paid per admission.
DC Not Mapped TANF Standard claims increased about $5.2M, with 119 more admissions and about $26.1K higher paid per admission.
DC also showed additional Not Mapped growth in ABD Non Dual and CHIP Standard, adding about $0.9M combined.
VA, TN, IN, and CO each showed smaller but recurring Not Mapped increases, confirming this is not isolated to one market.

business_patterns.top_pattern: Authorization code movement is a gating issue across multiple states
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: Prior-authorization coding and classification across CA, FL, IN, NY, TX, and VA
key_driver_codes: Postpartum and Postabortion Diagnoses without O.R. Procedures
Major Small and Large Bowel Procedures with CC
Cranial and Peripheral Nerve Disorders without MCC
business_patterns.pattern_details: Several states show cost movement tied to authorization code distribution rather than a clean utilization or reimbursement pattern. The issue touches rehabilitation, maternity, bowel surgery, pneumothorax, and nerve disorder episodes across both state- and provider-level views. These are validation cases first, because policy or provider action could be misdirected if the authorization flag moved or was reclassified.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: Authorization coding shifts can distort both UM targeting and financial attribution, creating false positives in trend investigations.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Reconcile prior-authorization flag logic and upstream file feeds across CA, FL, IN, NY, TX, and VA, then rerun business actions only after the coding movement is explained.
business_patterns.validation_reason: The pattern is explicitly driven by authorization code distribution shifts and is marked for validation before action.
evidence_summary: IN showed about $3.0M tied to authorization code distribution in Rehabilitation with CC/MCC.
NY added about $1.9M tied to authorization code distribution in postpartum cases.
TX added about $1.7M tied to authorization code distribution in major bowel procedures.
CA added about $1.6M tied to authorization code distribution across cranial/nerve and pneumothorax cases, with another $1.2M across FL and VA provider-level shifts.

business_patterns.top_pattern: IN rehabilitation spend is rising through both case mix and rehab setting growth
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: IN / Rehabilitation with CC/MCC across Physical Rehab, CHILDRENS, and ACUTE HOSPITAL
key_driver_codes: TRAUM SUBARACHNOID HEM LOC UNKN SUB
business_patterns.pattern_details: IN has a concentrated rehabilitation pattern that spans both clinical case mix and rehab-oriented sites of care. Aftercare, weakness, and other rehab-related diagnoses are increasing alongside operational growth in Physical Rehab and CHILDRENS settings across several products. Some segments are volume-led while others show higher paid per admission, so this needs coordinated clinical, UM, and payment review.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: This points to a service-line level rehab issue in IN rather than isolated claim noise.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Run an IN rehabilitation service-line review focused on admission criteria, aftercare placement, physical rehab utilization, and pediatric rehab pricing for Rehabilitation with CC/MCC.
evidence_summary: IN clinical rehab case mix added about $4.2M, led by aftercare diagnoses that contributed about $2.9M and 104 more admissions.
A separate weakness-related rehab pattern added about $765K with 46 more admissions.
IN ABD Non Dual Physical Rehab added about $862K from higher volume, while LTSS Non Dual Physical Rehab added about $465K with both volume and unit-cost pressure.
IN CHILDRENS rehab-related spend added about $749K combined across mixed and unit-cost patterns.

business_patterns.top_pattern: A small number of hospitals are disproportionately driving spend growth
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: Provider concentration at MAIMONIDES MEDICAL CTR and SENTARA NORFOLK GENERAL HOSPITAL
business_patterns.pattern_details: Provider concentration is visible in two different ways. In NY, MAIMONIDES MEDICAL CTR appears repeatedly across products in Not Mapped claims with higher admission activity and mixed cost pressure. In VA, SENTARA NORFOLK GENERAL HOSPITAL stands out for higher paid per admission in acute hospital claims even as admissions declined, indicating a different provider economics issue.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: A provider-level approach is more actionable here than broad market action because spend is concentrated in named hospitals with different underlying levers.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Open provider-specific audits for MAIMONIDES MEDICAL CTR and SENTARA NORFOLK GENERAL HOSPITAL, separating NY volume and classification issues from VA unit-cost and contracting review.
business_patterns.validation_reason: Much of the NY provider concentration sits in Not Mapped facility claims and should be confirmed before attributing the full increase to provider performance.
evidence_summary: MAIMONIDES MEDICAL CTR drove about $1.6M in NY TANF Standard Not Mapped volume growth, with 36 more admissions.
MAIMONIDES MEDICAL CTR added about $1.0M in NY ABD Non Dual Not Mapped claims and about $0.9M in NY Family Care Not Mapped claims.
SENTARA NORFOLK GENERAL HOSPITAL drove about $1.6M in VA TANF Standard acute hospital spend while admissions fell by 21, showing a clear unit-cost issue.
Across these two hospitals, the pattern spans both provider concentration and misclassified site-of-care exposure.

business_patterns.top_pattern: DC is showing a shift into non-acute settings, especially OTHER and long-term care hospital
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: DC Medicaid facility mix across OTHER, LONG TERM CARE HOSPITAL, Physical Rehab, and COMMUNITY MENTAL HEALTH CENTER
business_patterns.pattern_details: DC growth is not limited to acute hospital care. Spend is moving into OTHER, long-term care hospital, physical rehab, and community mental health center settings, with the largest increases in OTHER facility claims for TANF Standard and ABD Non Dual. Some settings are primarily volume-led, while long-term care hospital and mental health center episodes also show meaningful per-admission cost increases.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: This is a site-of-care management issue with multiple non-acute settings contributing to higher spend in DC.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Run a DC site-of-care review across OTHER, long-term care hospital, physical rehab, and community mental health center claims to confirm medical necessity, redirectable care, and setting-specific payment rules.
evidence_summary: DC TANF Standard OTHER facility claims increased about $2.2M with 104 more admissions and only minimal change in paid per admission.
DC ABD Non Dual OTHER facility claims added about $1.1M with 54 more admissions, again showing a strong volume signal.
DC TANF Standard long-term care hospital claims added about $519K with only 3 more admissions but about $23.8K higher paid per admission.
DC ABD Non Dual community mental health center claims added about $176K from a single additional admission with very high paid per admission, making it a targeted setting review item.

business_patterns.top_pattern: Rare catastrophic inpatient cases are creating sharp but low-volume spikes
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: FL, NY, TN, and UNATTRIBUTED low-volume catastrophic inpatient episodes
key_driver_codes: Tracheostomy with Mechanical Ventilation >96 Hours or Principal Diagnosis Except Face, Mouth and Neck without Major O.R. Procedures
Craniotomy and Endovascular Intracranial Procedures with MCC
Spinal Fusion Except Cervical with Spinal Curvature, Malignancy, Infection or Extensive Fusions with MCC
Septicemia or Severe Sepsis without Mechanical Ventilation >96 Hours with MCC
business_patterns.pattern_details: These increases come from a small number of very high-cost inpatient events rather than broad utilization growth. The pattern includes tracheostomy with prolonged ventilation, craniotomy, spinal fusion, sepsis, and a few unmapped rare cases across FL, NY, TN, and UNATTRIBUTED. Because the spend is concentrated in single admissions or very small runs, each case needs individual review rather than broad policy changes.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: A handful of catastrophic cases can materially move trend and need different action than routine utilization growth.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Perform single-case clinical and payment review on each high-cost admission to confirm severity, coding, and payment accuracy before escalating any broader policy response.
business_patterns.validation_reason: Most cases are single-admission or very low-volume outliers, and some include Not Mapped DRGs, so claim-level confirmation is needed before generalizing the trend.
evidence_summary: One DC tracheostomy with prolonged ventilation admission contributed about $1.3M by itself.
A single DC craniotomy case added about $667K, and rare provider-level spinal fusion and respiratory procedure cases added more high-cost outliers.
A separate sepsis subset across FL, NY, and TN added about $336K, mostly at MAIMONIDES MEDICAL CTR.
An additional Not Mapped rare-case group in TN and UNATTRIBUTED added about $107K and reinforces the need for claim-level review.

business_patterns.top_pattern: CA maternity complications are a distinct inpatient case-mix driver
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: CA inpatient maternity and postpartum episodes
key_driver_codes: Postpartum and Postabortion Diagnoses without O.R. Procedures
business_patterns.pattern_details: CA has a maternity-led inpatient complexity pattern centered on postpartum and puerperal complications. The increase is driven by both more admissions and higher paid per admission in severe pre-eclampsia and other postpartum complication cases. This is a distinct maternity action path and should not be managed as generic inpatient growth.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: Maternity complications have different clinical and care-management levers than general medical or surgical admissions.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Route CA postpartum cases for focused maternity review, including obstetric complication coding, case management escalation, and postpartum care pathway assessment.
evidence_summary: CA clinical case-mix change added about $2.4M overall.
Severe pre-eclampsia in postpartum cases contributed about $500K with 58 more admissions.
Other mental disorders complicating the puerperium added about $229K with higher paid per admission.
Puerperal sepsis added about $160K with 15 more admissions.

executive_summary.headline: The dominant story is authorized inpatient spend growth, but a large share of the signal is entangled with facility mapping gaps, authorization code movement, and a small number of concentrated providers and outlier cases.
executive_summary.primary_business_message: MO acute hospital TANF Standard growth is the largest direct cost pattern and should be addressed through joint utilization and reimbursement action. Before broadening policy changes, the plan should first resolve two gating data issues: Not Mapped facility claims and AUTH_CODE_DISTRIBUTION shifts. After that, the most actionable targeted levers are IN rehabilitation management, provider-specific action in NY and VA, and DC site-of-care review.
recommended_focus_order: Fix validation issues first: Not Mapped facility claims and AUTH_CODE_DISTRIBUTION shifts.
Address the largest confirmed operational pressure: authorized acute hospital growth led by MO and recurring in other TANF Standard markets.
Target concentrated service lines and providers next: IN rehabilitation, MAIMONIDES MEDICAL CTR, SENTARA NORFOLK GENERAL HOSPITAL, and DC non-acute site-of-care growth.

notes: All explicit authorization coding shift groups were consolidated into one gating validation pattern.
Not Mapped facility growth was kept separate from authorization code shifts because the downstream action is facility and provider reclassification rather than auth policy change.
Several smaller low-volume pediatric, acute hospital, and physical rehab groups under about $0.5M were left ungrouped to preserve a clear business story.
Left 13 analytical groups unassigned to preserve clean narrative attribution.
Segment attribution is weak for 39% of cards (43 of 109) on segment_by [service_area_state]; add those dimensions to the stage's dimension or carry-through list to attribute them at cell level.
Merged 22 immaterial segment group(s) into residual groups labelled with their literal segment values.
